title: Dark Fantasy
paragraphs: An early-1940s supernatural anthology of ghosts, curses, strange legends, and psychological horror, written and produced for radio by Scott Bishop.

Horror/suspense anthology written by Scott Bishop, originating at WKY Oklahoma City and moving to NBC network presentation in January 1942. Specialist chronology documents 31 programs; the frozen GRH set preserves 27, omitting 2, 22, 23 and 31. RadioGOLDINdex disagrees with the specialist log on the program number of the May 1, 1942 broadcast.
GRH documents the program through WKY local era (November 14, 1941 to December 26, 1941) and NBC network era (January 2, 1942 to June 19, 1942) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Scott Bishop (writer on 25 recordings, director on 1 recording, and host on 1 recording), Ben Morris (performer on 21 recordings), Tom Paxton (announcer on 19 recordings), Eleanor Naylor Caughron (performer on 16 recordings), Muir Hite (performer on 15 recordings), Fred Wayne (performer on 12 recordings), and Garland Moss (performer on 7 recordings).
The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network) and [[org|org.94ffaea84a0018ac|WKY]] (originated at station).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include horror and supernatural threat, suspense and mortal danger, death, murder and the dead, curses, superstition and occult belief, sea, ships and maritime mystery, and past, time and historical intrusion.
GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including WKY local horror anthology, NBC network transition, Sustaining network horror, and Incomplete survival of a 31-program run.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|pat-novak-for-hire|Pat Novak, for Hire]] (1 shared credited people) and [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]] (1 shared credited people).
